开篇原第1–4段连续裁切，保留A–J完整词表。NG34/35已核对整篇，原文并未给柏拉图所受批评或最早地球仪的准确性评价。

原文片段 · 1In 2008, Peter Bellerby, who lived in London, wanted to give his father a model globe for his eightieth birthday. What seemed simple enough to start with triggered an almost obsessive, decade-long journey, marked by a series of obstacles that would have deterred anyone less determined. It ended with his establishing the world's only bespoke globemaking company.

原文片段 · 2The first surprise in The Globemakers, Bellerby's account of this impulsive enterprise, is that obtaining such a globe was not simply a matter of a quick online order and a repressed sigh at the shipping costs. After all, contrary to stubbornly held popular views of our ancestors' geographical ignorance, we have known that the world is spherical since at least the 6th century BCE. The ancient Greek philosopher Plato in his work Phaedo likened it to a leather ball, while the accolade of producing the first recorded globe goes to the ancient Greek philosopher Crates of Mallus, who is said to have made one in around 150 BCE. Surely, Bellerby reasoned, a good-quality globe wouldn't be difficult to find.

原文片段 · 3Nearly two millennia later, however, it seemed that the art of globemaking had been largely forgotten. Bellerby came across shoddy commercial versions designed for school classrooms and genuine antiques in auction houses that would have bust his budget. Even his trips to Morocco and India, where surely the knowledge of artisan cartographers* had been preserved, drew a blank.

原文片段 · 4Not one to be easily thwarted, Bellerby decided to make his own good-quality globe. In the process, almost everything that could possibly go wrong did so. Even the shape of the Earth posed a problem, as it is not quite a perfect sphere, but oblate (slightly flattened at the poles). Having decided to compromise and opt for two half-spherical pieces that could be fitted together, he was unable to discover anyone capable of casting moulds with sufficient accuracy to ensure that he would not be left with two half-spheres that were not quite the same circumference. Even after he eventually resolved this issue, extracting these from the moulds resulted in piles of cracked plaster of Paris** and clouds of choking dust in the workshop he had set up at the rear of his house.

材料精读 · 内容与词句

一次寻找生日礼物的行动变成漫长的制球事业。作者用地球仪的悠久历史衬托现实中高质量成品和工艺人才的难寻，再具体展示模具精度及脱模问题，让制作困难有可理解的物质细节。

原文片段 · 1
In 2008, Peter Bellerby, who lived in London, wanted to give his father a model globe for his eightieth birthday. What seemed simple enough to start with triggered an almost obsessive, decade-long journey, marked by a series of obstacles that would have deterred anyone less determined. It ended with his establishing the world's only bespoke globemaking company.

2008年的最初目标只是给父亲八十岁生日买一个地球仪，后来却延伸成十年左右的执着探索和定制企业。what seemed simple 与 a series of obstacles 对照，把简单购买到复杂事业的反差放在开头；关于企业独特性的说法属于原文叙述。

原文片段 · 2
The first surprise in The Globemakers, Bellerby's account of this impulsive enterprise, is that obtaining such a globe was not simply a matter of a quick online order and a repressed sigh at the shipping costs. After all, contrary to stubbornly held popular views of our ancestors' geographical ignorance, we have known that the world is spherical since at least the 6th century BCE. The ancient Greek philosopher Plato in his work Phaedo likened it to a leather ball, while the accolade of producing the first recorded globe goes to the ancient Greek philosopher Crates of Mallus, who is said to have made one in around 150 BCE. Surely, Bellerby reasoned, a good-quality globe wouldn't be difficult to find.

作者插入古代已知地球呈球形及早期地球仪的历史，是为了说明 Bellerby 为什么以为好地球仪应该不难找。who is said to have made 保留对历史记载的转述性质。Surely 呈现人物当时的想当然，后文将让这一期待落空。

原文片段 · 3
Nearly two millennia later, however, it seemed that the art of globemaking had been largely forgotten. Bellerby came across shoddy commercial versions designed for school classrooms and genuine antiques in auction houses that would have bust his budget. Even his trips to Morocco and India, where surely the knowledge of artisan cartographers* had been preserved, drew a blank.

现成市场两端都不能满足需求：学校用商品粗糙，古董又超出预算。远赴摩洛哥和印度仍未找到所需帮助。drew a blank 表示一无所获；这里的 artisan cartographers 指具有地图制作手艺的人，不只是现代数字地图从业者。

原文片段 · 4
Not one to be easily thwarted, Bellerby decided to make his own good-quality globe. In the process, almost everything that could possibly go wrong did so. Even the shape of the Earth posed a problem, as it is not quite a perfect sphere, but oblate (slightly flattened at the poles). Having decided to compromise and opt for two half-spherical pieces that could be fitted together, he was unable to discover anyone capable of casting moulds with sufficient accuracy to ensure that he would not be left with two half-spheres that were not quite the same circumference. Even after he eventually resolved this issue, extracting these from the moulds resulted in piles of cracked plaster of Paris** and clouds of choking dust in the workshop he had set up at the rear of his house.

自己制作后，困难从地球并非完美球体开始，一直延伸到两半球周长一致和完整脱模。他选择近似球形是一种折中，但即使解决模具精度，石膏仍会破裂并产生粉尘。段落强调设计决定、制作精度与材料操作是不同层面的难题。

词语与搭配
marked by a series of obstacles

伴随一连串障碍

marked by 概括过程的显著特征；需要后文具体事件支撑，不能只用来空泛说事情困难。

contrary to stubbornly held popular views

与人们固执持有的流行看法相反

contrary to 引出认识反差；stubbornly held 带有评论者对观念不易改变的评价。

drew a blank

没有找到所需结果

固定表达，描述寻找过程无果，语气较生动；不是画出空白图形。

with sufficient accuracy

具有足够精度

原文指模具精度必须达到两半球周长相合的要求，sufficient 与具体用途有关。

句子精读
What seemed simple enough to start with triggered an almost obsessive, decade-long journey, marked by a series of obstacles that would have deterred anyone less determined.

起初看似再简单不过的一件事，却开启了一段近乎执着、长达十年的探索，其间一连串的障碍足以让决心稍弱的人退缩。

What 从句整体作主语，指寻找地球仪这件事。marked by 补充 journey 的特征；that would have deterred 修饰 obstacles，用假设语气反衬 Bellerby 的坚持，不是叙述另一个真实退缩者。

Even after he eventually resolved this issue, extracting these from the moulds resulted in piles of cracked plaster of Paris** and clouds of choking dust in the workshop he had set up at the rear of his house.

即使他终于解决了这个问题，把半球从模具中取出来时，仍在房屋后方自己搭建的工作间里留下成堆开裂的熟石膏和令人呛咳的粉尘。

this issue 回指两半球尺寸精度不一致，these 指半球件。extracting these from the moulds 是动名词短语作主语。Even after 表明先前难题解决并不代表整个过程顺利；he had set up 修饰 workshop。星号沿用材料中的注释标记。
